subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class browser-plugin config for per-profile proxy settings plus per-agent/subagent browser-profile binding, or should this remain external orchestration through remote CDP, multiple gateways, node-host profiles, or ClawHub-style packages?
rationale: The missing capability is source-confirmed, but implementing it defines public config, browser egress policy, proxy credential handling, and agent/session ownership semantics that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Design Core Browser Contract
options.body: Approve a first-class browser-plugin design for proxy secrets, per-agent inheritance, concurrency limits, tab ownership, and diagnostics before implementation.

options.title: Split Remaining Work
options.body: Keep this as the umbrella while the broader proxy issue owns transport/security policy and the subagent browser issue owns attachment and operator-visibility semantics.

options.title: Defer To External Orchestration
options.body: Document remote CDP, multiple gateways, browser-lock-style wrappers, or ClawHub packages as the supported path and close only after maintainers decide not to add core config.

recommendation.title: Design Core Browser Contract
recommendation.body: Approve a first-class browser-plugin design for proxy secrets, per-agent inheritance, concurrency limits, tab ownership, and diagnostics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the browser profile config, browser plugin ownership, docs, and security-sensitive browser control paths.
